title: An infinite sequence of higher order Ehrenfest transitions in a one-dimensional crystal
authors: Sakineh Mizani, Szabolcs Varga, Martin Oettel, Péter Gurin
abstract: Higher-order Ehrenfest phase transitions are exceptionally rare and poorly understood. We present an exactly solvable one-dimensional model exhibiting a sequence of Ehrenfest transitions of arbitrary $n\geq2$ order. These transitions occur without symmetry breaking and even the second-order transition lacks conventional critical behavior, although the density derivative of the correlation length diverges. Our results reveal a distinct class of noncritical phase transitions and help clarify the scope of the Ehrenfest classification.
summary: This work presents a theoretical study of a 1D hard-sphere crystal exhibiting an infinite sequence of higher-order Ehrenfest phase transitions. By analyzing the free energy via the transfer operator and DFT, the authors prove that these transitions are marked by discontinuities in the $n$-th derivative of the free energy, rather than conventional critical divergences. This clarifies the scope of Ehrenfest classification for non-critical, geometrically driven transitions.
main_problem: The paper investigates the existence and nature of higher-order Ehrenfest phase transitions ($n \ge 2$) in a confined, one-dimensional crystalline system.
main_result: It demonstrates an infinite sequence of phase transitions characterized by a discontinuity in the $n$-th derivative of the free energy, confirming a distinct class of noncritical phase transitions.
method: The analysis employs the transfer operator method and Density Functional Theory (DFT) to calculate the free energy by solving eigenvalue problems across different density regimes.
model_or_system: The system is a one-dimensional solid composed of hard spheres confined by a periodic external potential, modeled using concepts from statistical mechanics and lattice physics.
key_observables: Free energy ($f$), its derivatives ($f^{(n)}$), positional correlation length ($\xi$), and the local density profile ($ho(x)$).
important_parameters: Density ($ho$), lattice constant ($\ell$), sphere diameter ($\sigma$), and the transition order ($n$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the system's thermodynamics can be determined by the dominant eigenvalue of the transfer operator, and that the free energy is analytic within fixed density regimes.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the non-analytic connection of eigenvalue branches, the discontinuity of free energy derivatives at transition points, and the evolution of the density profile $ho(x)$ across different regimes.
paper_structure: The paper builds from the general transfer operator formalism to specific calculations using DFT for the grand canonical ensemble, culminating in the derivation of the free energy and the identification of the order of the phase transition via derivative discontinuities.
why_interesting: While focused on classical statistical mechanics, the rigorous mathematical framework of identifying non-critical transitions via derivative singularities is highly relevant to understanding phase transitions in quantum many-body systems where conventional critical exponents might fail.
